title: Grandia III
subtitle: A would-be pilot meets someone with another calling

body: Grandia III is Game Arts' PlayStation 2 role-playing game, first released in Japan on 4 August 2005. Yuki dreams of becoming a great pilot in a world where aircraft use magical power. Meeting Alfina, who can communicate with the world's Guardians, carries that ambition into a much larger journey. The player travels with a changing party through a story that connects flight, family and spiritual danger. The series' familiar interest in adventure is expressed through movement between places, while its battle system makes the timing of actions important within each encounter.

The combat timeline shows the approach of allied and enemy actions, allowing the player to judge which attack or technique can intervene at a useful moment. Position and timing turn a selected command into part of a larger sequence rather than an isolated exchange. Guardians offer further help as the campaign progresses. Between encounters, Yuki's aircraft replaces a conventional walking world map, with new landing points opening as the story advances. The player's expanding ability to travel therefore remains visible, connecting a young pilot's ambition to the practical structure of reaching the next part of the adventure.

Hidenobu Takahashi directed the game, with returning series composer Noriyuki Iwadare supplying the score and Miz performing the opening song In the Sky. Much of the team had worked on earlier Grandia releases. North America received the game in February 2006, while Europe did not receive an original edition. Reviews were generally favourable, particularly towards the combat system. Grandia III carries forward the series' way of making battle timing readable, placing that carefully ordered rhythm beside a story whose protagonist is eager to rise above his starting point and discover a wider world.
